prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1121; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A dated repair quote from before the policy start shows this same damage already existed.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the claimant, who states they were a passenger in a vehicle struck from behind at a stop. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer and has been advised of the claims process.

Entry 2: Police attended the scene and their report confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision. Several bystanders who stopped at the scene also confirm this.

Entry 3: Photographs supplied by the policyholder show damage to the rear of the vehicle consistent with the reported impact. No independent witnesses have come forward to describe the collision itself.

Entry 4: The driver, who lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member, gave a statement that matches the claimant's account of how the impact happened.

Entry 5: The claimant reported shoulder pain on the day of the collision and was assessed at an urgent care clinic. The injury described is consistent with the force and direction of the impact shown in the vehicle damage.

Entry 6: An inspection of the vehicle found damage to the rear bumper, tailgate, and surrounding panels that matches the described impact. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known to this office from its records.

Entry 7: A repair estimate issued before the policy start date shows that damage of this same type and location already existed on the vehicle. This conflicts with the other information gathered so far and is being reviewed with the policyholder.

Entry 8: Medical records received show the claimant has no prior treatment or complaints involving the same shoulder. No earlier injury to that area is known.

Entry 9: The claimant has described the collision the same way in each conversation, including the initial call, the recorded statement, and a follow-up call. Details such as the speed and the sequence of events have stayed consistent.

Entry 10: Treatment followed a typical course, with physiotherapy and medication over several weeks. The claimant's reported pain has eased steadily as treatment progressed, and the treating provider has noted improvement.

Entry 11: The treating provider has indicated that treatment is tapering off as the claimant recovers. The claimant has been asked to provide any further records and to confirm whether symptoms have fully resolved.

Entry 12: Based on the medical records, the photographs, the police report, and consistent statements, the injury appears genuine and proportionate to the collision. The prior repair estimate remains open for further review before a settlement decision is made.
